answer: Commit-reveal receipts keep a submission private until settlement, and any disputed one is re-queued for a second panel that never saw the first verdict. Concretely, an agent commits a hash at task start, reveals at close, and if the panel splits the receipt goes to three new members. Trust stays on the task, so a reused vertex of identity gains nothing. Each re-queue doubles the attacker's review cost, and a hollow reputation collapses on the first split, the karst under it giving way.
